subject: MAP: Glenwood Analytics — Performance benchmark plan & quantization regressions
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@glenwood-analytics.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: MAP proposal + performance benchmark plan (latency/TTFT/concurrency + quant)

Alice —

Thanks for the productive call earlier. Per our agreement, attached is a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that focuses on performance benchmarks you requested: latency (P50/P95), throughput at target concurrency, TTFT (time-to-first-token), and regression checks for quantized kernels (FP16/BF16 vs INT8/INT4). High-level proposal below; the attached PDF has the timeline and acceptance criteria.

Goals (what we will measure)
- P50/P95 latency at 1, 5, 20 concurrent request lanes (ms)
- Sustained throughput (tokens/sec) at target batch sizes
- TTFT baseline and after batching/kv-cache warm-up (ms)
- Model quality/regression checks: top-1 token perplexity on your evaluation corpus and task-specific pass rates
- Kernel profiling: operator-level time breakdown (matmul, attention, softmax, layernorm) across FP16/BF16 and INT8/INT4 paths

Evaluation plan (technical)
- We will run three parallel pipelines:
  1) Baseline FP16 full-precision run (reference)
  2) BF16 variant where available (hardware permitting)
  3) Quantized INT8 and aggressive INT4 variants with per-layer calibration and post-quantization evals
- Each run will include: cold-start TTFT (first request), warmed KV-cache scenario (steady-state), and concurrency stress ramps.
- Regression checks: automated comparison against your provided eval set; fail criteria = >3% drop in task pass rate or >5% increase in perplexity for any quantized variant.

Operational plan and MAP milestones
- Week 0: Sign-off MAP + provide evaluation corpus and SLAs (you)
- Week 1: Redwood runs baseline and quick sanity tests; share preliminary kernel-profile snapshot
- Week 2: Quantization runs + tuning (INT8); preliminary impact report
- Week 3: INT4 experiments (if requested) + final recommendation; prepare canary rollout plan
- Week 4: Sign-off and deployment scheduling / procurement handoff

Attachments: gw_map_draft_20270220.pdf (MAP draft with milestones).

Can you confirm the evaluation corpus path and whether you require INT4 experiments or if INT8 is the initial target? If you're ok with the proposed timeline we'll start baseline runs Monday.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MAP proposal + performance benchmark plan (latency/TTFT/concurrency + quant)

Hannah —

Thanks, this looks thorough. We can provide the evaluation corpus (20K anonymized prompts + 2K QA checks) via the secure bucket link by EOD Tuesday. INT8 is our priority; INT4 would be exploratory but please run if it’s low-effort. Key asks from our side:
- Please include a per-route SLA target (P95 < 250ms) and a suggested concurrency headroom number for 99% availability.
- We need the kernel breakdown so our infra team can map GPU type to expected cost.

Available for a quick sync on Wednesday at 11am PT if you want to walk through the MAP.

Regards,
Alice Turner
Head of ML Engineering, Glenwood Analytics

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Feb 2027 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: RE: MAP proposal + performance benchmark plan — early run notes + artifacts

Team —

We completed the first-pass baseline and INT8 calibration runs against the Glenwood corpus on our nvX2 fleet. Summary of early findings (see gw_bench_results_v1.csv for full numbers):

Summary (high level)- Baseline FP16: P50 = 60ms; P95 = 180ms at concurrency=5; TTFT cold = 240ms; steady-state throughput = 3.2k tokens/sec per instance.
- INT8 (per-layer quantization w/ calibration): P50 improved ~10% (54ms); P95 improved ~12% (159ms); throughput +14%; TTFT cold roughly unchanged (+/- 5%).
- INT4: runs completed but quality regressions observed on a subset of QA checks. Per our regression criteria, INT4 shows a 6-8% drop in task pass rate on the provided QA set — recommend NOT promoting INT4 to canary at this time.

Kernel profile notes (operator-level time percent of total token time)- FP16: matmul 46%, attention 30%, softmax+norm 12%, others 12%
- INT8: matmul 34%, attention 34%, softmax+norm 14%, other 18% — we see reduced matmul time but attention stays significant due to KV-cache patterns

Actionable recommendations- Proceed with INT8 canary for customer acceptance testing (CAT).
- Add additional prompt calibration step for the top-3 problematic QA items before rolling canary.
- Record per-route traces during canary to validate P95 under mixed traffic.

Attachments: gw_bench_results_v1.csv (214KB), gw_map_timeline_v2.pdf (updated milestones).

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP proposal + performance benchmark plan (summary & next steps)

Alice —

Looping you in with a short summary of the concrete next steps and our recommended MAP updates after the early runs (quoted below). In short: INT8 is the recommended path to meet your latency/throughput goals while keeping quality within your tolerance. INT4 shows regressions and we recommend pausing on it unless you want an investigative track.

What we need from Glenwood to start the INT8 canary (target Week 2 of the MAP):
- Confirm approval to run INT8 canary against 5% production-like traffic (you can opt for a mirrored traffic approach if preferred).
- Sign off on the canary acceptance criteria: P95 <= 200ms, no >3% drop on task pass rate, and no critical QA failures on the selected 2K checks.
- Confirm procurement timeline for reserved capacity if you want guaranteed throughput during ramp.

If you approve, we will:
- Lock the canary config (INT8 with per-layer calibration) and push the rollout policy into the MAP timeline (see attached gw_map_timeline_v2.pdf).
- Start per-route tracing and automated regression checks (we’ll share a dashboard link).

Thanks — can you reply with a single-line approval or a requested change? We need sign-off to keep the Week 2 target.

Best,
Hannah
